situation:
You are the financial analyst for RIDGELINE CONNECT COOPERATIVE, a rural telecommunications provider owned by the people who work in it. Every technician, installer and office employee holds an equal share, and the general manager (judge) reports to them. The general manager (judge) has asked you to study a partnership offer that arrived this month and to recommend whether the cooperative should accept it.

RIDGELINE CONNECT COOPERATIVE sells internet and phone service to about nine thousand households across three counties. Nearly all of its spending is fixed. The fiber lines, the switching equipment and the loan payments on both cost the same whether one household subscribes or all nine thousand do. Those fixed costs set a pricing floor of roughly forty dollars a month, below which no plan covers its share of the network.

NORTHBEAM WIRELESS, a national carrier, has offered a five-year agreement to lease capacity on the cooperative's fiber. The payments would finish the remaining fiber build in four years rather than eight and let RIDGELINE CONNECT COOPERATIVE hold residential rates steady. Accepting the lease would also let NORTHBEAM WIRELESS set the wholesale price, approve future network upgrades, and put its name on the network — control the member-owners have held since they founded the cooperative.

Turning the offer down leaves every pricing and upgrade decision with the member-owners. It also means raising residential rates well above the pricing floor and stretching the fiber build to eight years, and the cooperative expects some subscribers to leave for a satellite competitor while they wait. The general manager (judge) wants you to explain the pricing floor, forecast the cash flow under each course of action, and recommend one.

You will present your analysis and your recommendation to the general manager (judge) in the general manager's office. The general manager (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas. After your presentation and your answers to the general manager's questions, the general manager (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the general manager of RIDGELINE CONNECT COOPERATIVE, the rural telecommunications provider owned by the people who work in it. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You want the financial analyst to explain how the cooperative's fixed costs set the pricing floor, to forecast cash flow both under the NORTHBEAM WIRELESS lease and without it, and to recommend one course of action. You will consider either recommendation, provided the analyst can show what it costs the member-owners.

After the presentation you will ask these two questions:
judgeQuestions: What would be your first step in carrying out your recommendation?
How would you explain this decision to the member-owners at the annual meeting?
